description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/column_nonuniform_1d/rules/entraining_plume_lev driven by model PlumeTrapezoidal of problems/plume_column_trapezoidal.esm: the accumulator w(1) equals the lowered plume phi exactly, so the L2 error of w at t = 1 against phi* = 1 + sin(pi z) isolates the trapezoidal step, expected O(dz^2) on the stretched column with the VARYING entrainment rate lam = 2 + 3z (a frozen-coefficient step would show order 1 here).

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.python: Measured 2026-11-14 against EarthSciAST main bf7c1fa2: earthsci_ast rejects the problem before simulating with `observed_cycle: models/PlumeTrapezoidal: observed definition cycle: phi -> phi`. Its structural observed-cycle check runs on the PRE-lowering equation phi = entraining_plume_lev(phi_env, lam, src, phi0, phi), where phi appears as a bare argument, so the esm-spec 4.3.1.1 self-edge exemption (which looks for an index(phi, ...) read) does not apply; after the 9.6.3 rewrite the RHS is the recurrence faq reading index(phi, k-1), which julia and rust accept and evaluate. Python's lowered AST for this rule is byte-identical to the julia golden (tests/conformance/ast/entraining_plume_lev), so only the pre-lowering cycle check blocks it. The python conformance job is also disabled on main for runtime (.github/workflows/conformance.yml). Re-arm once the check runs on the lowered equations.
